note: N 탓이다 = it's N's fault; 탓에 = because of (bad result).

ex.en: It's my fault. I'm sorry.
Because of the weather, the plane left late.
I told the kids not to blame others.

note: Verb: 실패하다 (to fail).

ex.en: It's okay if you fail. You can try again.
The first bread I baked was a total flop.
This project ended in failure.

note: 짜증(이) 나다 = be annoyed; 짜증(을) 내다 = snap at someone.

ex.en: The traffic is so bad, it's annoying.
Don't snap at me.
I get cranky when I'm hungry.

note: Someone who started before you. Opposite: 후배.

ex.en: A senior colleague bought me lunch.

ex.s: 지우 선배는 저보다 두 학년 위예요.
ex.en: Ji-woo is two years ahead of me in school.
I asked an upperclassman for travel tips.
Can you speak Japanese?
The menu is written only in Japanese.
These days I'm learning Japanese with an app.
Our team won the championship!
My son won the swim meet.

ex.s: 회사 축구 대회에서 우리 부서가 우승했어요.
ex.en: Our department won the company soccer tournament.

note: Often 천사 같다 = angelic, so kind.

ex.s: 우리 아기는 잘 때 천사 같아요.
ex.en: Our baby looks like an angel when she sleeps.
Thanks for helping. You're a real angel.
That nurse was a real angel.
I'll go buy ingredients for kimchi stew.
It's delicious because the ingredients are fresh.
I bought supplies for my kid's art class.

note: Verb: 편집하다 (to edit).

ex.en: I'm editing my travel video.
What photo editing app do you use?
I do magazine editing at my company.
On the weekend we went strawberry picking as a family.
I picked tomatoes in the yard.
I finally got my driver's license last year.
I forgot my account password.

ex.s: 가족이랑 영화 앱 계정을 같이 써요.
ex.en: I share a movie app account with my family.

ex.s: 회사 이메일 계정이 아직 안 만들어졌어요.
ex.en: My work email account hasn't been set up yet.
It's quite cold today.
That restaurant is quite expensive.
Your Korean has improved considerably.
We're late anyway, so let's take it slow.
I'm throwing it out anyway, so just take it.

ex.s: 어차피 비 오니까 집에서 영화 봐요.
ex.en: It's raining anyway, so let's watch a movie at home.
What time exactly are we meeting?
Please tell me the exact address.

ex.s: 의사 선생님한테 증상을 정확히 말해야 돼요.
ex.en: You need to describe your symptoms precisely to the doctor.

note: Konglish; also 휴대폰. Very common in speech.

ex.en: My phone battery is almost dead.
I left my phone at the restaurant.

ex.s: 아이한테 아직 핸드폰은 안 사 줬어요.
ex.en: We haven't bought our kid a phone yet.

note: A slightly stronger form of 아마.

ex.en: It'll probably rain tomorrow.

ex.s: 민호는 아마도 아직 회사에 있을 거예요.
ex.en: Minho is probably still at the office.

ex.s: 아마도 다음 달에 이사할 것 같아요.
ex.en: We'll probably move next month.

note: Verb: 경쟁하다 (to compete).

ex.en: Competition at that company is really fierce.
Competition between cafés around here is intense.
There's a lot of competition between the brothers.

en: in one's own way; depending on
note: Often 나름대로; N 나름이다 = it depends on N.

ex.en: I prepared hard in my own way.
Taste depends on the person.
This neighborhood is pretty nice in its own way.

note: 허가(를) 받다 = to get permission.

ex.en: You need permission to take pictures here.

ex.s: 부모님 허가 없이는 캠프에 못 가요.
ex.en: You can't go to camp without your parents' permission.
We finally got a business permit for the store.
I checked the weekly weather forecast.
There's a weekly meeting every Monday.

ex.s: 간호사인 친구는 이번 달에 주간 근무만 해요.
ex.en: My nurse friend only works day shifts this month.
That employee's attitude was really unfriendly.
Attitude matters in an interview.
My son's attitude in class has gotten much better.
Don't suddenly approach a dog you don't know.
Let's approach this problem differently.
They say a typhoon is approaching.

note: Verb: 번역하다 (to translate).

ex.en: Could you help me translate this sentence?
I read the menu with a translation app.
I do English translation work at my company.
Open your books to page 30.
We spread out a mat in the park and sat down.
We unfolded the map and found the way.

note: Often 하루 종일.

ex.en: It rained all day.
I was in meetings all day today.
I rested at home all day on the weekend.
They say there's a high chance of rain tomorrow.

ex.s: 이 수술 성공 확률이 얼마나 돼요?
ex.en: What's the success rate of this surgery?

ex.s: 그 버스를 탈 확률은 거의 없어요.
ex.en: There's almost no chance we'll catch that bus.
I looked at the clock and it's already ten.
I got a watch as a birthday present.
How much is this watch?
What level are you in this game?
I took a level test for Korean class.
This hiking trail is beginner level.
The problem at work has been completely solved.
The internet problem hasn't been fixed yet.
The money issue has been resolved now.
Medical terms are so hard.
What does this term mean?
I'm still not used to the company jargon.
The visa application process is complicated.
Please tell me the refund procedure.
Where do I go to get admitted?

note: Casual variant of 예쁘다; both are standard.

ex.en: This dress is really pretty.
The baby is so cute.
The café is decorated really nicely.
Just tell me the key points briefly.
The key to dieting is consistency.
Before the test, I memorized just the key words.
Why are people staring at me?
The kid keeps staring at the ice cream.
He's been staring at his phone all day.
The letters are too small for me to see.
I memorized all the Hangul letters.
The text came through with garbled characters.

note: Verb: 공유하다 (to share).

ex.en: Could you share the photos?
I shared the meeting materials with my team.

ex.s: 온라인 수업에서 화면 공유가 안 돼요.
ex.en: Screen sharing isn't working in the online class.
Please don't touch the paintings.
You shouldn't handle the fruit too much.
Can I pet your dog?
I'm gradually increasing my workout time.
The company gave us more vacation days.
Please lengthen these pants a little.

en: to step forward, intervene; to set out

ex.en: Nobody would do it, so I stepped up.
Don't get involved in your friends' fight.
I left the house early in the morning.
Our next-door neighbor gave us rice cakes.
We had dinner with our neighbors.
I left my package with a neighbor.
My shoulder really hurts.
My shoulders are stiff from using the computer so long.
I carried the bag on my shoulder.

en: section (of a store); segment (of a show)
note: Konglish trap: not a street corner (that's 모퉁이).

ex.en: Where is the fruit section?
I bought a book in the bookstore's children's section.
That show's cooking segment is fun.

note: Used with -지만 / -아도: 비록 작지만.

ex.en: Although it's small, I like our home.
Even though we lost, it was fun.
Although it's expensive, the taste is the best.

en: excessive, too much; to pass by
note: 지나치게 = too much, excessively. As a verb: to pass by.

ex.en: I think that's a bit too much.
Exercising excessively is bad for your body.
The bus went right past our stop.
I'm really anxious because the exam is coming.
I'm uneasy because my kid isn't home yet.
I get a little anxious every time I fly.

note: Often dismissive: 그런 거 따위 = stuff like that.

ex.s: 그런 말 따위 신경 쓰지 마세요.
ex.en: Don't pay attention to talk like that.
I don't need stuff like this.
Money and such isn't important.
The internet is so slow.
Service at this restaurant is a bit slow.
I'm a slow walker.

en: to stack, pile up; to build up

ex.en: I piled the moving boxes in the living room.
The kids stacked the blocks up high.
I built up a lot of experience at that company.

note: Takes -에: N에 속하다.

ex.en: Which team are you on now?
I belong to the school band.
Does a tomato count as a fruit?
I'll prove it with my skills.
Do you have ID to prove your age?

ex.s: 제 말이 맞다는 걸 증명해 볼게요.
ex.en: I'll prove that I'm right.
I'll pray that you do well on your test.
Grandma prays every morning.
We prayed for the surgery to go well.

note: For today's weather, use 날씨.

ex.en: It's nice here because the climate is warm.
I caught a cold because the climate is different.

ex.s: 이 식물은 더운 기후에서 잘 자라요.
ex.en: This plant grows well in hot climates.
Do you have this in a bigger size?
What size coffee would you like?
My kid's shoe size went up again.

note: The alphabet; the language itself is 한국어.

ex.en: Hangul is easy to learn.

ex.s: 간판에 한글이랑 영어가 같이 쓰여 있어요.
ex.en: The sign is written in both Hangul and English.
I added Hangul to my phone keyboard.
What would you like to order?
I ordered a book online.
Shall we order chicken for dinner tonight?

note: 댓글(을) 달다 = to leave a comment.

ex.s: 제 사진에 댓글 달아 줘서 고마워요.
ex.en: Thanks for commenting on my photo.
Don't worry too much about the comments.
According to the comments, this restaurant is good.

ex.s: 이 상자 좀 같이 들어 줄래요?
ex.en: Could you help me lift this box?
I put the gift in a pretty box.
I bought a box at the post office.

note: Also common: N 예정이에요 (it's planned).

ex.en: The meeting is scheduled for three o'clock.
The wedding is planned for next month.
The surgery has been scheduled for tomorrow morning.
I broke a glass at the café.
There's a crack in the car's windshield.
Glass bottles have to be thrown out separately.

note: Formal; in conversation 병 is more common.

ex.en: Does this insurance cover illness too?

ex.s: 손을 자주 씻으면 질병을 예방할 수 있어요.
ex.en: Washing your hands often can prevent disease.

ex.s: 여행 전에 그 나라 질병 정보를 확인하세요.
ex.en: Check that country's health risks before you travel.
Look over the lease carefully.
The doctor examined my throat.
I'm slowly looking around the store.
I think I've caught a cold after all.

ex.s: 아무래도 오늘은 못 갈 것 같아요.
ex.en: I don't think I can make it today after all.
A bigger car is just more comfortable.
I found my passport right before leaving.
It's right before the exam, so I'm really nervous.
Don't look at your phone right before bed.

note: Used as 적극적으로 (actively) or 적극적인 N.

ex.en: Participate actively in class.
Minsu is really proactive at work.
He was the one who eagerly reached out first.
I watched an animated movie with the kids.
Do you like Japanese animation?
I majored in animation in college.
Could you tie my hair up?

ex.s: 등산 전에 신발 끈을 꽉 묶으세요.
ex.en: Tie your shoelaces tight before hiking.
I tied up the luggage with string.
The birthday party theme is dinosaurs.
We went to a theme park on the weekend.
I changed my phone's theme.
Sorry I haven't been in touch for so long.
I worked at that company for a long time.

ex.s: 이 식당 앞에서 오랫동안 줄을 섰어요.
ex.en: We stood in line outside this restaurant for a long time.

note: 옳아요 is pronounced [오라요].

ex.en: Minho is right.
It's right to tell your friend the truth.
I'm not sure what's right.

note: Verb: 발견하다 (to discover, find).

ex.en: I discovered a great restaurant in the neighborhood.
The problem was found early in the checkup.
I found money while sorting my clothes.

note: Going camping is 캠핑.

ex.en: My kid went to summer camp.
I signed up for an English camp over the break.
I made lots of friends on the first day of camp.
The baby reacts to sounds.
Nobody reacted to my joke.
My skin reacted to this cream.
The new air conditioner has been installed.
The app wasn't installed properly.
A new printer was installed at the office.
My daughter starts middle school next year.
I met my middle school friends after a long time.
Is there a middle school near here?

en: to be satisfied, be happy with
note: Takes -에: N에 만족하다.

ex.en: I'm very happy with the new house.
Were you satisfied with the service?
Are you happy with your current salary?
Ji-woo has a talent for drawing.
I guess I have no talent for cooking.
I want to nurture my child's talent.

note: ㄹ-irregular: 돌아요, 도세요, 도는.

ex.en: Turn right at the next intersection.
I walked one lap around the park.
A cold is going around these days.
I often watch movies by myself.
I come to this restaurant from time to time.
I call my parents now and then.
Don't try to trick me.
That store cheated us on the price.
There are a lot of phone scams that trick people.

note: The flame itself is 불; 화재 is a fire incident.

ex.en: Last night there was a fire at a local restaurant.
The fire alarm went off, so everyone went outside.
Do you have fire insurance on your house?
I sent the documents by mail.
A wedding invitation came in the mail.
How much is the postage?
I lost the flow of the conversation.
The pacing of the movie is a bit slow.
I don't know much about current fashion trends.
I'm a college student studying in Seoul.
Is there a discount for college students?
Our son is a college student now.
The meeting time has been changed.
The flight's gate has changed.
My phone number has changed.

en: to think over, worry about, agonize
note: Noun: 고민 (worry); 고민 중이에요 = I'm thinking it over.

ex.en: I'm trying to decide what to eat.
I'm torn about whether to change jobs.
Don't agonize over it too long, just buy it.

en: indeed, as expected; I wonder if

ex.en: It really is as delicious as people say.
Seoul really does have a lot of people.
I wonder if we can really finish by tomorrow.

en: altogether; (not) at all; from the start

ex.en: I'll just start over from the very beginning.
I don't eat meat at all.
I just turned my phone off altogether.

note: ㅂ-irregular: 부드러워요.

ex.en: This meat is really tender.
I like this towel because it's soft.
The teacher spoke to me gently.

note: 운이 좋다 = lucky; 운이 나쁘다 = unlucky.

ex.en: You're lucky today.
Luckily, I got the last ticket.
Tests are about skill, not luck.

en: to endure, hold out, get by

ex.en: Hang in there a little longer and it's the weekend.
How do you get through this heat?

ex.s: 이 돈으로 한 달 버틸 수 있어요?
ex.en: Can you get by for a month on this money?

note: In conversation, 미국 사람 is more common.

ex.en: I'm an American from Chicago.

ex.s: 우리 회사에 미국인 직원이 두 명 있어요.
ex.en: There are two American employees at our company.
This restaurant has a lot of American customers.
This song is widely known.
This medicine is widely used.
Word has spread far and wide that that restaurant is good.

note: Verb: 도전하다 (to take on, try).

ex.en: This year I'm going to take on a marathon.
Want to try the spiciest ramen?
Taking on a new job scares me.

en: to be ahead; to come before
note: N에 앞서 = before N.

ex.en: Our team is leading 2 to 1.
Mom walked on ahead.
Before the meeting, let me briefly say hello.

ex.s: 선생님이 이 부분을 여러 번 강조했어요.
ex.en: The teacher emphasized this part several times.
The doctor stressed exercise.
The team leader stressed the deadline.

en: to hug, hold in one's arms
note: Not 알다 (to know). Forms: 안아요, 안아 주세요.

ex.en: Do you want to hold the baby?
I hugged my mom tight at the airport.
My friend was crying, so I gave her a hug.

note: 르-irregular: 저질러요.

ex.en: I made a big mistake at work.
The kid got into trouble again.
I made another impulse purchase.
I'm going downtown to shop this weekend.
How long does it take to get downtown by bus?
I met a friend downtown.

note: N 위주로 = mainly N, focusing on N.

ex.en: These days I eat mostly vegetables.
This test focuses on grammar.
On the trip we went mainly to good restaurants.

note: Job title: 김 대리님. 대리(운전) = designated-driver service.

ex.en: Assistant Manager Park is in a meeting right now.
My husband was promoted to assistant manager this year.
We've been drinking, so let's call a designated driver.
